articles.title: Nosebleeds: recognising when professional help is needed
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: A nosebleed can follow irritation, illness or injury; appearance alone cannot establish the cause.
Record whether there was a fall or impact and whether other symptoms are present.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Heavy or persistent bleeding, or a person becoming unwell, needs prompt professional assessment.
Seek emergency assistance for severe symptoms rather than relying on unreviewed treatment advice.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Tell a clinician when bleeding began and whether this has happened before.
Mention relevant medicines or bleeding conditions if known, without guessing.

articles.title: Possible concussion after a head impact: information for responders
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: A head impact can cause problems even without an obvious external wound.
Record the mechanism and any changes in memory, awareness, speech or behaviour.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Increasing drowsiness, seizures or other severe symptoms warrant emergency assessment.
Do not use this draft to decide that a head injury is safe to monitor at home.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Share the approximate time and circumstances of the impact.
Describe reported changes without attempting a diagnosis.

articles.title: Suspected sprain or joint injury: recognising assessment needs
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: Pain and swelling after a twist or fall can have several causes, including fracture.
Describe which joint was affected and whether the person can use the limb.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Severe pain, deformity or numbness warrants urgent assessment.
Do not attempt to reposition a joint using an unreviewed diagram.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Record when and how the injury occurred and how symptoms changed.
A clinician can determine appropriate investigation and follow-up.

articles.title: Blisters and skin friction: recognising problems beyond routine discomfort
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: Blisters may follow friction, pressure or other skin irritation; causes differ.
Note the location and whether burns or chemicals were involved.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Spreading skin changes, fever or substantial pain should prompt medical advice.
This draft does not instruct on puncturing, draining or dressing blisters.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Record approximate onset and relevant activity or footwear.
Describe changes to a clinician while protecting personal privacy.

articles.title: Insect stings: distinguishing local observations from emergency warning signs
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: A sting may cause local discomfort or a more serious reaction.
Record the approximate time and suspected insect without approaching a nest.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Breathing difficulty, collapse or rapidly developing widespread symptoms are emergencies.
Contact emergency services promptly and follow any existing individual care plan.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Tell responders the symptom timeline and known allergies if confirmed.
Do not delay help to identify the insect or inspect the sting.

articles.title: Animal bites: information to share when seeking assessment
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: Bites can cause injury or infection even when visible marks appear small.
Record the animal type and circumstances without attempting to catch it.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Deep injury, significant bleeding or serious illness needs prompt assessment.
Ask a clinician about wound evaluation and relevant infection considerations.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Share the time and setting of the bite and verified animal details.
Do not speculate about infection status or expose private information.

articles.title: Fever and worsening illness: recording useful observations
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: A raised temperature is only one observation and cannot establish a diagnosis.
Note changes in behaviour, breathing, drinking and ability to communicate.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Confusion, unresponsiveness or severe breathing problems require urgent assessment.
Babies and medically vulnerable people may require earlier professional advice.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Record actual readings with device and time when available.
Share a concise timeline without delaying urgent care to complete it.

articles.title: Vomiting and diarrhoea: recognising when an illness needs assessment
articles.summary: Draft recognition and communication guide; not a treatment protocol.
articles.illustration_review_note: Any clinical illustration requires qualified review; no procedural diagram supplied.

sections.title: Recognise and describe
paragraphs: Vomiting and diarrhoea have many causes; frequency alone does not determine severity.
Record onset, associated symptoms and whether the person is becoming weaker.

sections.title: When to seek help
paragraphs: Blood, severe pain or altered consciousness requires urgent medical advice.
Young children, older adults and medically vulnerable people may need earlier assessment.

sections.title: Information for professionals
paragraphs: Keep a short timeline and any professional instructions already received.
Protect privacy and follow applicable current public-health guidance.
